evidence.observation: Repository discovery is owned entirely by GitRepo. The constructor takes candidate fnames (or git_dname), resolves each to an absolute path, and calls git.Repo(fname, search_parent_directories=True).working_dir to find the enclosing repository. It de-duplicates discovered working dirs, raises FileNotFoundError when none exist and errors when more than one repo is found, then pins self.repo and self.root to the single repo. It also records the optional aider_ignore_file path here, so both discovery and ignore configuration are bound to this class rather than to RepoMap.

get_tracked_files is the boundary where discovery is combined with ignore rules. It walks commit.tree.traverse() (cache in self.tree_files), adds staged index entries, normalizes paths with normalize_path, and then applies the final filter: `res = [fname for fname in files if not self.ignored_file(fname)]`. The list it returns is therefore already git-discovered and ignore-filtered; downstream consumers (e.g. RepoMap) receive plain filenames and never touch git or ignore logic themselves.

refresh_aider_ignore implements the .aiderignore side of the ignore policy. It short-circuits when no aider_ignore_file is configured, rate-limits checks to once per second, and uses the file mtime to decide whether to reload. On reload it clears ignore_file_cache and compiles the file's lines into self.aider_ignore_spec via pathspec.PathSpec.from_lines(GitWildMatchPattern, lines). This isolates ignore-rule parsing/caching inside GitRepo.

ignored_file_raw is the actual ignore predicate. It first enforces subtree_only by confining paths to the current working directory (returning True for paths outside cwd, including on the ValueError path from issue #1524), then returns False if no .aiderignore exists, and otherwise normalizes the path and returns self.aider_ignore_spec.match_file(fname). Together with ignored_file (caching) and git_ignored_file (git's own .gitignore check via self.repo.ignored), all ignore evaluation lives in repo.py.

RepoMap construction takes only presentation/limits configuration: map_tokens, root, main_model, io, repo_content_prefix, refresh, and map_mul_no_files. It sets up the tags cache (load_tags_cache), tree/map caches and timing state. There is no git import, no GitRepo reference, and no file discovery here, confirming that map construction is deliberately decoupled from repository discovery.

get_repo_map is the public entry point and it receives the file universe as explicit arguments: chat_files and other_files (plus mentioned_fnames/mentioned_idents). It computes a token target, delegates ranking to get_ranked_tags_map, and prepends repo_content_prefix. It never enumerates the repository itself, so callers must supply an already-discovered, already-ignore-filtered file list.

get_ranked_tags is where the map graph is actually built. It unions chat_fnames and other_fnames into `fnames`, checks each is a real file on disk, computes personalization scores from chat membership and mentioned idents, extracts tags via get_tags (tree-sitter), aggregates defines/references/definitions, builds a networkx MultiDiGraph, and runs pagerank. The only filesystem work is reading the filenames it was handed; there is no discovery or ignore-rule evaluation.

get_ranked_tags_map_uncached converts ranked tags into a token-budgeted map. It merges special_fnames (from aider.special.filter_important_files applied to other_fnames), then binary-searches the tag prefix length, rendering candidates with to_tree and measuring them with token_count until the result fits within max_map_tokens (15% error tolerance). Its input is a ranked tag list, so it stays purely in the map-construction domain.

claims.claim: Repository discovery is centralized in aider/repo.py: GitRepo.__init__ resolves every candidate fname to its enclosing git working directory via git.Repo(search_parent_directories=True) and enforces that exactly one repository is involved, setting self.repo and self.root. aider/repomap.py contains no git import or GitRepo usage, so RepoMap cannot and does not discover repositories itself.

Ignore rules are applied entirely inside aider/repo.py. GitRepo.get_tracked_files collects files from the git tree plus the staged index and then filters them through self.ignored_file; ignored_file caches results and delegates to ignored_file_raw, which enforces subtree_only cwd confinement and matches the compiled .aiderignore spec, while git_ignored_file separately consults git's own ignore rules. Consequently the filename list handed to RepoMap is already ignore-filtered.

Map construction in aider/repomap.py is decoupled from discovery and ignore logic. RepoMap is constructed with only root/token/model configuration, and get_repo_map/get_ranked_tags_map/get_ranked_tags/get_ranked_tags_map_uncached all take chat_fnames and other_fnames as parameters; RepoMap only reads those files to extract tags and rank them, never enumerating or filtering the repository.

The separation boundary is the filename list. base_coder.get_all_relative_files() calls self.repo.get_tracked_files() (discovery + ignore already applied) and get_all_abs_files() turns those into absolute paths; base_coder.get_repo_map then partitions them into chat_files and other_files and passes them to self.repo_map.get_repo_map. Repository state and ignore policy live on GitRepo while RepoMap consumes only the resulting file names.

conclusion: The two modules implement a clean, one-directional separation. aider/repo.py owns everything stateful about the repository: discovery (GitRepo.__init__ locating a single git working tree from candidate paths and defining self.root) and ignore policy (refresh_aider_ignore parsing .aiderignore with pathspec, ignored_file/ignored_file_raw enforcing subtree_only and pattern matching, git_ignored_file delegating to git), with get_tracked_files combining git tree + staged index enumeration and then filtering via ignored_file to emit the authoritative file list. aider/repomap.py owns only map construction: RepoMap is initialized from root/token/model configuration with no git dependency, accepts chat_files/other_files as explicit arguments, reads those files to extract tree-sitter tags in get_ranked_tags, builds a pagerank-weighted reference graph, and fits the rendered tree to a token budget in get_ranked_tags_map_uncached. The handoff is the already-discovered, already-ignore-filtered filename list produced by GitRepo.get_tracked_files and passed through base_coder into RepoMap.get_repo_map; RepoMap never calls git and repo.py never builds a map. One caveat: repomap.py's module-level find_src_files helper is a fallback used only by its __main__ block and is not part of the normal wired path.

validation.notes: All eight cited symbol/line-range pairs verified with ast: GitRepo.__init__ 62-129, get_tracked_files 433-488, refresh_aider_ignore 500-521, ignored_file_raw 542-565, RepoMap.__init__ 47-87, get_repo_map 103-167, get_ranked_tags 365-574, get_ranked_tags_map_uncached 629-706 all reported OK. grep confirmed aider/repomap.py has no git import or GitRepo reference (only two incidental error-string mentions of 'git' at lines 144 and 415), and that ignore filtering is wired in repo.py at line 486 (get_tracked_files) with matching at line 565 (ignored_file_raw). No test suite was run because this is an explore task with no code changes; the source files were not modified.
